content.comment_body: Hello! I'm experiencing significant challenges getting an analog signal to register on my [product_name]. I've reviewed multiple forum discussions and tutorials, but none address my specific situation. For testing, I'm applying a 5V signal from a simple voltage regulator circuit and attempting to view the value on the device's display (expecting around 500 according to the 0-1000/0V-10V scaling). However, the display persistently shows 0. My wiring setup includes +24V power to P1 (sourced from [product_name] and protected by a 1A fuse), and the commons are connected accordingly. The +5V from my regulator circuit goes to I7, with the common ground linked to [product_name]. A ladder diagram is attached. I plan to test analog output from an IR sensor next, but I can't advance unless I can read a simple input first. Any help is appreciated.

Hello [user_name]! Unfortunately, the [product_name] you are using, even though it operates on 24V DC, doesn't natively support analog inputs in the way you're expecting. Only certain models such as the 12/24RC (and its variants), and other versions are able to handle 0-10V analog signals on specific digital inputs. For analog inputs with your [product_name], you'll need to use an additional analog module capable of accepting two channels of either 0-10V or 0/4-20mA signals. Take care!

analysis.insight_summary: Users encounter difficulties obtaining analog input values on [product_name] due to built-in hardware restrictions. Despite consulting multiple guides and forums, true analog readings don't appear on the display, pointing to a lack of clear documentation regarding hardware capabilities. Community advice clarified the need for an external analog input module to achieve direct analog measurement functionality.
analysis.user_expectations: User anticipates [product_name] should accept analog voltages on digital inputs and directly display scaled values (0-1000) without additional hardware or complexity.
pain_keywords: lack of clear product limitation info
